notes:
RMM agent: remote administration (rmm module): manage Windows and Linux endpoints from the browser. With agent
1.8.0, the endpoint page adds the *Processes*, *Services*, *Files*, *Terminal*, *Scripts*, *Logs*, *Registry*
(Windows), *Remote desktop* and *Activity* tabs, and a menu to reboot or shut down the computer.

- Processes and services: processes with their user, CPU, memory, path and command line; end them (also forced,
  or with their child processes) and start programs as SYSTEM/root or as the logged-in user. Critical system
  processes ask for an extra confirmation. Start, stop and restart Windows services and systemd units and change
  their start type.
- Logs and Windows Registry: the Windows event logs (Security only with its own permission) and the Linux journal
  and syslog files, filtered by date, level, source, event ID and text, and the agent's own log to view or download.
  On Windows, browse and change Registry keys and values of every usual type; sensitive keys are protected and
  administrators can protect more.
- Terminal: PowerShell, CMD or Bash in the browser, as SYSTEM/root or as the logged-in user. It survives a short
  connection drop, closes after 30 idle minutes (configurable) and, when closed, ends everything started from it.
- Files: browse drives and folders, create folders, rename and delete. Downloads and uploads of any size show
  progress and speed, resume by themselves after a dropped connection or a page reload and are checked with SHA-256.
  Administrators can limit the folders that can be used.
- Scripts (*RMM → Scripts*): a library of PowerShell, CMD, Bash and sh scripts with parameters (secret ones are
  never stored in clear) and versions that can be compared and restored. Only a signed version that has not expired
  can run (signing can set an expiry date), and the agent refuses a script changed after it was signed. Each run
  shows the output live and records the exact version and SHA-256 that ran.
- Bulk actions: in *Inventory → Endpoints*, select endpoints (or pick them by site, tag or filter) and run a
  script, reboot or shut them down, start, stop or restart a service, or collect the agent logs. The confirmation
  shows how many endpoints are affected and how many are online; the others get the job when they connect, until it
  expires (24 hours by default). *RMM → Tasks* shows the result on each endpoint, cancels what is pending and retries
  what failed.
- Remote desktop in the browser (RDP): *Connect via Remote Desktop* opens a window with the screen of a Windows
  endpoint: resolution, full screen, Ctrl+Alt+Del, shared clipboard and automatic reconnection. It goes through the
  agent to the computer's own Remote Desktop service, so no RDP port has to be opened on the network; if that service
  is off, *Enable Remote Desktop* turns it on. You sign in with a Windows account every time (nothing is stored) or
  with a credential from the vault; Microsoft accounts (an e-mail address) may fail, so use a local or domain
  account. Windows Home cannot receive connections; on Windows 10 and 11 the connection opens its own session instead
  of showing the user's screen; one monitor and no sound; the clipboard needs NetPilot over HTTPS.

RMM security:

- Permissions per action (*RMM → Permissions*): one permission per tool and action. By default read-only users
  only look; editors also use the terminal, files (without deleting), processes, services, scripts on one endpoint,
  reboot and remote desktop; administrators can do everything. Existing editors get these defaults when you upgrade,
  so review them. Each permission can be allowed or denied per role or per user, also only on some sites, and the
  server checks them on every action.
- Confirm your identity: terminals, scripts, bulk actions, changes on an endpoint, signing scripts, permissions,
  security settings, the emergency switch and (by default) remote desktop ask for your password or 2FA code again,
  valid for 10 minutes (*RMM → Settings → Security*). Users without a local password (single sign-on) need 2FA. API
  tokens cannot confirm an identity, so these actions cannot be done with an API token.
- Activity log (*RMM → Activity* and on each endpoint): every action, also the failed and denied ones, with user,
  address, target, result, exit code, duration, output and script version and hash; CSV export, kept for 365 days by
  default and also shown in the endpoint's change log history.
- Emergency switch (*Disable remote actions* on the *RMM* page): at once refuses new terminals, remote desktop
  sessions, uploads, scripts, bulk actions and changes, closes the open sessions and cancels pending and running
  jobs; viewing keeps working, and the agents enforce it even without a connection. A banner across the app shows who
  turned it on and why.
- Usage limits per user (script runs and destructive actions per minute, endpoints per bulk action, terminals,
  transfers and remote desktop sessions at once), changeable per role or user. Every order to an agent is signed,
  expires and is accepted only once.
- Update the agents: these tools need agent 1.8.0. Endpoints with an older agent show *Update the agent*:
  reinstall it from *RMM → Deploy agent* (it keeps its identity and its data). Keep NetPilot on a single process
  (NETPILOT_WORKERS=1, the default): the live tools reach an agent through the process it is connected to.

RustDesk (second remote-desktop option): technicians can also reach Windows and Linux endpoints with their own
RustDesk client. NetPilot bundles RustDesk 1.5.0, third-party software under the AGPL-3.0 shipped unmodified as a
separate program (NetPilot is not affiliated with its authors): every server package carries its official installers
for Windows x64 (MSI) and Linux x64/ARM64 (deb and rpm), its license and the source links, also shown on the license
page and in docs/THIRD-PARTY.md.

- Settings (*RMM → Settings → RustDesk*, administrators; off by default): RustDesk's public servers or your own
  ID and relay servers (hbbs/hbbr) with their public key, and whether the connection link includes your server and
  the password. *Apply to N endpoints* updates the endpoints that use other server settings.
- Install, update and uninstall from the new *RustDesk* tab of an endpoint, or on many at once from
  *Inventory → Endpoints*. The agent downloads the package from its own NetPilot server (never from the internet),
  checks its size and SHA-256, installs it silently, applies the server settings and sets a permanent password; on
  Windows, RustDesk keeps its Start-menu shortcut and its icon next to the clock, visible to the user, and on Linux
  apt or dnf install its dependencies from the distribution's repositories. Uninstalling also deletes RustDesk's ID
  and password on the computer by default. One RustDesk operation runs on an endpoint at a time, and cancelling or
  the emergency switch take effect between installer steps.
- Connect with RustDesk: a dialog with the RustDesk ID, a rustdesk:// link that opens the technician's client
  (with the password and, if chosen, your server), copy buttons and the RustDesk client to download from NetPilot
  itself. The endpoint does not need to be online.
- Permanent password: 24 characters generated by the server, stored encrypted, sent only inside the signed,
  encrypted job and never written to logs, job output, the activity log or the change log; NetPilot's process lists
  hide it. *Rotate password* sets a new one in one click.
- Permissions: new permission *Remote desktop with RustDesk* (rmm.rustdesk; editors and administrators by
  default). Installing, configuring, rotating the password, uninstalling and connecting ask you to confirm your
  identity, are blocked by the emergency switch and are recorded in the activity log and in the change log. It needs
  agent 1.8.0.
- Limitations: RustDesk only accepts the permanent password on its command line, so process auditing or security
  software may record it (on Linux, other local accounts may see it while it is being set unless /proc is mounted
  with hidepid=2); turn off *Include the password in the link* to copy it instead. The emergency switch does not
  close open RustDesk sessions, and uninstalling the NetPilot agent leaves RustDesk installed. Not supported: Windows
  on ARM64, Linux without a graphical session (on Wayland the user has to accept sharing the screen), SUSE, macOS and
  a RustDesk server inside NetPilot.

Warehouse (new stock module, in the Operations, MSP and Enterprise licenses; *Inventory → Warehouse*): stock of
cables, equipment and spare parts in several warehouses, each serving one or more sites and with bins (shelves).

- Items with SKU, barcode, category, unit (also meters with decimals), cost, supplier, photo and minimum stock,
  tracked by quantity or by serial number (each unit with its asset tag, status, assignee and the endpoint or device
  where it is installed).
- Movements (receipt, issue, transfer, adjustment, return, check-out and check-in) in a ledger that is never edited:
  a mistake is corrected with a compensating movement, stock never goes below zero, not even with two scans at the
  same time (unless an administrator turns on *Allow negative stock*), and a retried request is never applied twice.
- QR labels on A4 sheets or Brother and thermal rolls (the field module is not needed) and a Scan page for
  the phone camera or USB/Bluetooth scanners: +1/−1 in one tap, continuous mode and undo.
- Stock counts (also blind and from several phones at once), low-stock notifications, CSV import with a dry run and
  export, and per-site permissions.

Software licenses (*Inventory → Warehouse → Licenses*, with stock or with finance): the company's software
licenses (Microsoft 365, Windows, antivirus, SaaS…), in the same list as in *Costs & contracts*, with encrypted keys,
expiry, renewal and end of support. Seats are assigned to people and/or to endpoints and devices, and released,
reassigned or burned (OEM), with their history; assignments never go over the purchased seats. *Licenses* tab on
endpoints and devices, a people view with offboarding, expiry and seat notifications, and CSV import and export.

Documentation (new docs module, in the Auditor, Operations, MSP and Enterprise licenses; new *Documentation*
section of the menu): the IT team's knowledge base, organized like a wiki in shelves, books, chapters and pages.

- Visual editor with tables, task lists, callouts, code, images, embedded PDFs and files; automatic drafts, a notice
  when someone else is editing the same page, conflict detection and the history of each page (the last 100 versions
  by default) to compare and restore.
- Seven built-in templates in English and Spanish (site documentation, network runbook, onboarding, incident
  post-mortem, change plan, installation record and meeting notes) and your own, with variables.
- Import Markdown, HTML, text, Word (.docx), PDF and whole books in ZIP; export to HTML, Markdown, text and ZIP, and
  print to PDF.
- Pages are linked to sites, devices, endpoints, racks, circuits, VLANs, prefixes, IP addresses, WiFi networks,
  credentials, stock items and tickets (also with @ mentions) and appear in the *Documentation* tab of each object
  and in the search.
- Each book is visible to everyone, only to users without site restrictions or only to one site; drafts only to those
  who can edit the book; recycle bin (emptied after 30 days by default). The change log, the journal, the dashboard's
  recent activity and the assistant hide the entries of pages a user cannot see (drafts they cannot edit, pages in
  the recycle bin or deleted).

AI assistant: changes mode (ai module): with *Allow the assistant to propose changes*
(*AI assistant → Settings*, off by default), editors and administrators can ask it to create, change or delete
locations, racks, devices, endpoints, interfaces, cables, IP addresses, prefixes, VLANs, WiFi networks and circuits
within their sites and, with their modules, warehouse items and movements, documentation pages and license seats.

- Nothing is applied without your confirmation: each proposal shows the changes field by field, with warnings,
  *Apply* and *Cancel*, and expires after 15 minutes. *Apply* checks your permissions again and that the record has
  not changed since.
- Undo for 7 days, from the chat or from the new *Changes* tab. The change log records these changes with the new
  source *AI assistant* and the user who confirmed them as the author.
- With stock, docs or finance, the assistant also looks up stock, documentation and software licenses.
- Fixed: the first message of a new conversation got no answer until you sent another one.

Endpoints: new type *Payment terminal* for card terminals (Ingenico, Verifone, PAX…), which discovery also
recognizes; card terminals already documented as *POS terminal* keep that type until you change it. The RMM agent can
now only be deployed on servers, desktop PCs, laptops, virtual machines and POS terminals: for the other types
*Deploy agent* is disabled, bulk remote actions leave them out and NetPilot never links an agent to them (an endpoint
with an agent cannot be changed to one of those types).

Discovery: new option *Always classify random MACs as mobile* (*Discovery → Adoption rules*, off by default):
hosts with a random (locally administered) MAC get the *Mobile phone* type whatever the other signals say, because
phones and tablets change their MAC for privacy. Hosts that answer SNMP and types set by hand or by a rule are not
changed. It applies at once to what has already been discovered and "Why this type?" shows it.

User manual (PDF) in English and Spanish inside NetPilot: open or download it from *Help & tutorials*, the user
menu, the welcome tour or the search (Ctrl+K), also without internet access. It is installed with every server
package and attached to every release.

Costs & contracts (finance module): users limited to some sites now only see the contracts, licenses and
budgets of their sites; those linked to no site, and budgets for the whole organization, are only visible to users
without site restrictions, and the totals match the rows each user sees. Each contract, license or budget they save
has to be linked to one of their sites. If you have such users, link the contracts and licenses they need to their
sites.

Credentials and Floor plans (vault and floorplans modules): users limited to some sites now only see the
credentials linked to a device, location, circuit, WiFi network or endpoint of their sites, and the floor plans of
their sites: also when revealing or copying, editing, deleting, exporting, in the access log, in the documentation, in
the client portal and in the client view. They do not see links to objects of other sites, which are kept when they
save. Credentials without links and floor plans without a location are only visible to users without site
restrictions. Each credential they save has to stay linked to something of their sites, and only users without
restrictions create, rename and move vault folders. Deleting an object removes its credential links. Undoing an
assistant change removes them too, a link to an object they can see but not change is only removed by someone who
can change it, documentation pages, exports, search and the assistant say *Hidden object* instead of the name of an
object the reader can't see, and the PDF of floor plans with zones no longer fails. If you have such users, link the
credentials they need to their sites.

Other changes: *Show key* on a software license or a seat adds an entry to the license's change log (who and
when, never the key). A circuit's contract end shows in *Costs & contracts → Renewals* and notifies 30 and 7 days
before, unless the circuit is already in a contract that renews. A circuit's termination device has to be in the
circuit's location or in one inside it. Duplicating a documentation template creates "Copy of …". *Warehouse → Scan*
searches by words, in any order. The *Stock state* column of the items follows the same rule as the low stock
warning.

Licenses: stock and docs are new modules. A license carries the modules it was issued with: to use them with
an Operations, MSP or Auditor license issued before 1.8.0, ask for an updated license (Enterprise licenses already
include every module). *Warehouse → Licenses* also works with finance alone.

Help and demo: help articles in English and Spanish for every new page and tab. The public demo includes sample
warehouses, documentation, software licenses, payment terminals and endpoints with RustDesk.

Releases: every server package includes RustDesk 1.5.0 (installers, manifest.json, NOTICE.txt
and RustDesk-LICENCE.txt) and the user manual, so the packages are larger (about 135 MB more for RustDesk and about
60 MB for the manual). A release build fails if a RustDesk installer is missing or does not match its pinned SHA-256,
or if a manual is missing. Each GitHub release also attaches the RustDesk source code of that version and the two
manual PDFs.

Dependencies: the server adds nh3, mammoth and markdown-it-py (Documentation), installed with the update;
the web app bundles TipTap, lowlight, highlight.js and DOMPurify (documentation editor and safe display), xterm.js
(terminal) and the IronRDP web client (remote desktop).

Database: migrations 0014 (RMM live tools, scripts, jobs, permissions and activity), 0015 (changes from the
AI assistant), 0017 (warehouse), 0018 (documentation), 0019 (software licenses and seats), 0020 (RustDesk
state of each endpoint) and 0021 (removes credential links to objects already deleted); they are applied
automatically when upgrading. Updating from the web takes a backup first;
if you upgrade by hand, take one with netpilotctl backup before.
